en.title: Number of Course Schedules with Limited Consecutive Classes
en.description:
Schedule exactly P physics classes and C chemistry classes so that the same subject never appears more than N times in a row; find the number of distinct subject sequences modulo 1000000007. Each line is an independent test, and classes of the same subject have no individual identities.

The standard input/output format and examples were compiled by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains T, followed by T lines of P C N. Full source ranges: 1≤T≤100, 1≤P,C,N≤1000.
en.output: Output T integers in input order, one result per line, each modulo 1000000007.
en.explanation: The example outputs are 2, 1; and 0 2 respectively.
hints: Count by runs of the same subject: F(s,k) is the number of ways to split s into k positive integers in 1..N. Group all tests by N and, based on the estimated amount of computation, choose between the inclusion-exclusion formula and a shared sliding-window DP; all s with the same N share one DP pass instead of being recomputed per test. Finally combine the cases where the run counts of the two subjects are equal or differ by 1.
